text.p: The following are the main stories from Monday morning's Austrian newspapers:
- Currently two petitions, one against gene-manipulation and the other for women's rights, are poised to become the most successful in the country's history.
- Maria Rauch-Kallat, general secretary of the conservative People's Party, wants to open the party to more liberal-minded voters.
- Interior Minister Karl Schloegl is thinking of changing parts of the new foreigner law due to harsh criticism.
- The U.S. secret service CIA bugged rooms of a Vienna hotel to listen in on OPEC delegations from Iran and Iraq, current affairs magazine Profil said.

- Austria's largest builder Bau Holding is expanding abroad to compensate for the bad economic situation at home. The firm has received an order to build 250 million schillings' worth of motorway in Italy.

- Motor engineer Steyr-Daimler-Puch looks to Asia for improving its business. The company plans to offer engineering to Indian and Chinese companies while talks with South Korean car maker Hyundai are also proceeding.
- Chancellor Viktor Klima says a reduction in work hours will only take place in tandem with a reduction in wages.

- The Transport Ministry has only found one bidder for Austria's third mobile phone network. Connect, the only interested party, sees massive start-up hinderances as the reason behind a lack of interest. The ministry still hopes to receive at least three offers.

- Bawag bank and insurer EA-Generali are expected to jointly bid for the government's stake in postal savings bank PSK. Insurer Wiener Staedtische is now seen not wanting to make an offer for the bank together with insurance holding BARC.
- Civil servants plan to resist plans by the government to continue austerity measures in the civil service, as Klima wants to reduce dramatically the number of employees.
- Chamber of Labour chief Werner Muhm demands Unilever expand production in Austria should it go ahead with the closure of one production facility as profits are very high anyway.
- Oil and chemicals group OMV plans to restart a project to supply Italy with gas via Croatia.
- Bank Austria plans to merge its foreign activities with Creditanstalt's, which it took over in January.
- Swiss pharmaceuticals group Hoffmann La-Roche will create 150 jobs by investing two billion schillings in its research facility in northern Austria.
